title: Asking the Moon About Its Wrinkles! The Story a Shrinking Moon Won’t Tell
part1:
The Moon has wrinkles, too. So let’s ask, “Mr. Moon, you’ve shrunk quite a lot, haven’t you?” But this witness will not tell us the whole story so easily. This study is a space detective story. It follows clues carved into the Moon’s face.

First, let’s look at the scene. The wrinkles are cliffs with one steep side and one gentle side. Scientists think they formed when pieces of bedrock pushed against each other. One piece moved up over the other. The team mapped these cliffs using camera pictures. Then they worked backward to estimate how much the Moon had shrunk.

The estimate was that the Moon’s radius had shrunk by about 42 to 46 meters. The Moon’s wrinkles are surprisingly exact witnesses.
part2:
But it is too soon to run the headline, “The Moon’s Shrinkage Fully Solved!” These numbers show shrinkage during a later part of the Moon’s history. Relatively young faults recorded it. They do not show the total shrinkage from the Moon’s birth to today. The diary we seized had no full record from the very beginning.

The difference from model results makes the case harder. This estimate is lower than what a model predicts for a cooling, shrinking Moon. But the model shows the total shrinkage built up over time. The numbers do not cover the same time or use the same method. So we cannot say, “The model is our confirmed suspect!”

What could explain the difference? The research team raised one possibility. A thick layer of loose rock, with gaps in it, may cover the Moon’s surface. It may have kept heat inside the Moon, making it harder for heat to escape. Could the Moon have worn a thick coat after all? Its “coat” of loose rock may have slowed how fast the Moon cooled and shrank.
part3:
Another possibility is that the Moon’s surface held back its report. Strong, springy bedrock may have kept faults from forming near the surface until enough force built up. In other words, shrinking did not always make wrinkles appear right away. “There was a change, but it did not show on the surface.”

Did the Moon cool in a different way? Or did something happen before its shrinkage turned into wrinkles? The reason for the difference is still unknown.

The Moon’s wrinkles are important witnesses, but they cannot speak for every time in its history. We should value what they tell us, but also notice what they do not say. To study the Moon’s face, we need more than a great detective’s sudden insight. We also need to check the evidence carefully.
in_one_line: Young faults on the Moon suggest its radius shrank about 42 to 46 meters later, not over its whole history. Its wrinkles tell only part of the story, and scientists do not know why this estimate differs from models.
